title: micro-feedback-queue-scratch - Eli
content:
Purpose: quick, portable notes for triaging small PR reviews that I expect to do in 15-30 minute bursts. Not a polished checklist — rough heuristics, quick-code ideas, and explicit follow-ups to avoid losing context in async review windows.

Context: backlog of tiny PRs that keep piling up (hotfixes, small refactors, doc fixes). I want a repeatable mental model to decide: quick-merge, needs work, or needs design/RFC. Also capture candidate refactors where a single line change suggests a bigger cleanup worth scheduling.

Quick triage rubric (15m):
- Safety: does this change touch auth, billing, or data paths? If yes -> stop, assign SRE/security + request more tests.
- Surface area: files touched <= 4 and tests included -> candidate for quick-merge.
- Behavior change: any change in public API/route/response schema -> needs design sign-off and changelog entry.
- Perf-sensitive: any code on hot path (inference runtime, batching, KV cache) -> add perf regression checklist and run locally with load-capture.

Merge outcomes:
- Quick-merge (green): small clarifying rename, docs, non-behavior tests, single-file lint fixes.
- Defer & label (needs-work): flaky tests, missing assertions, ambiguous error handling. Add labels: needs-repro, needs-tests, api-change, perf-risk.
- Block & escalate: security/privilege change, customer-impacting rollback, migrations. Ping owner + SRE/product.

Refactor ideas (when spotted):
- Repeating pattern: "if (x) return default; else ..." appears in 3 places in serving/runtime/route_parsers -> propose small util parseOrDefault(req, key, default) w/ unit tests. Low-risk, submit PR that only extracts identical logic.
- Duplicate prometheus instrumentation snippets in handlers/ -> centralize into metrics/middleware with standard labels (model, route, status) to simplify dashboards.
- Long method in optimize/quantize/selector.py (~220 lines): sketch -> split into select_kernel + score_by_latency + fallback_graph. Keep behaviour identical, add tests for each subcomponent.

Quick code sketch (notes to self for PR author):
- In route_parsers: prefer explicit type hints on helper functions (-> Optional[str]) to reduce my head-scratching.
- Replace repeated try/except KeyError with dict.get + explicit validation to avoid masking other exceptions.

Tests checklist to require before approving:
- Unit: new logic branches covered (happy path + 1 error case).
- Integration: small end-to-end on local dev (use small model stub) if change touches runtime path.
- Regression harness: add to ci/eval - if changed behaviour affects tokenization or sequence length, add a small regen test.

Follow-ups / TODOs (create tickets):
- FEAT-? : consolidate route parsing helpers (owner: Eli, estimate 1 day).
- OPS-? : add standard metric labels and update dashboard queries (collab: Ivy).
- TECHDEBT-?: split long quantize selector file, include bench microtests (collab: Rohan).

Example review comments (copy-paste snippets):
- "Can you add a unit test that asserts the fallback path is exercised? I want to avoid silent behavioural changes in prod"
- "Please move this instrumentation into the shared metrics helper so we keep labels consistent across handlers."
- "Why is this silent except/continue pattern used here? It masks errors (see case in X) — prefer explicit handling or rethrow with context."

Notes-to-self:
- When I mark "quick-merge", still add one sentence in PR explaining risk acceptance (no perf/regressions expected). Helps post-merge blameless debugging.
- Keep a running list of repeated patterns I keep extracting — if I extract the same helper twice, schedule a small cleanup sprint.

Open questions for reviewers:
- Is there an invariant about request.metadata keys we assume here? If so, should we add a typed wrapper?
- For the metric labels: do we standardize on 'model' or 'model_name'? Check existing dashboards before renaming.

Slack shortcuts I use while triaging:
- slow: "<owner> quick triage: small change, fine to merge if tests pass"
- block: "<owner> blocking: needs design/Security sign-off because <reason>"

End notes: this doc is intentionally terse. Copy any checklist bits into PR descriptions so the next reviewer has a clear signal. If I'm blocked > 24h on a single PR, escalate to the team's review rotation and create a tiny ticket with the triage notes above.

Recent PRs I used this on: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4823 (extracted metrics helper), https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4970 (small parser rename).

Last quick thought: try to keep PRs below ~120 lines of functional change; above that threshold, default to "needs-design" and ask for split suggestions.
